headline: STLLR GOLD DRILLS 13.00 g/t Au OVER 22.75m AT JONPOL — TIMMINS CAMP STRIKE EYES EXTENSION FROM 400m TO 1,200m
source_name: Junior Mining Network / STLLR Gold Inc. (TSX: STLR) — June 18, 2026
snippet: STLLR Gold Inc. (TSX: STLR) reported additional assay results from its 2026 drill program at the Jonpol Deposit within the Garrison Property of the Tower Gold Project in Ontario's Timmins Mining Camp on June 18, 2026 — with the best-in-program hole returning 13.00 g/t gold over 22.75 metres and a companion hole delivering 3.01 g/t gold over 22.93 metres, both from near-surface geometry confirming the high-grade, open-pittable character of the Jonpol system. The 2026 program has completed 8,536 metres of its first-half drilling budget, with assay results still pending for remaining holes. The program's primary objective is to test the western extension of Jonpol's open-pit mineralisation: the current Tower Gold Preliminary Economic Assessment defines mineralisation over approximately 400 metres of strike, and the 2026 program is specifically designed to test whether that strike can extend to approximately 1,200 metres — a three-fold increase that would proportionally expand the resource base ahead of a full feasibility study. The Timmins Mining Camp has produced over 70 million ounces of gold historically — the highest-output gold district in Canada — and Jonpol's combination of 13.00 g/t over 22.75 metres and shallow geometry positions it as an open-pit development candidate in a proven infrastructure corridor at the current $4,100-$4,200 gold price. For retail investors evaluating TSX-listed gold developers with active 2026 drill programs, each 100-metre westward extension of Jonpol's mineralised zone adds incremental ore tonnes at grades that generate cash margins exceeding $3,000 per ounce at the current gold price — making the strike-extension thesis directly translatable into PEA economics.

headline: FREEGOLD DRILLS 336.8m AT 1.32 g/t Au FROM NEAR SURFACE AT GOLDEN SUMMIT — 6-RIG 50,000m ALASKA CAMPAIGN ROLLS TOWARD 2027 PFS ON 30 MOZ DEPOSIT
source_name: North of 60 Mining News (June 19, 2026) / Freegold Ventures Limited (TSX: FVL)
snippet: North of 60 Mining News reported on June 19, 2026 that Freegold Ventures Limited (TSX: FVL) is releasing a steady stream of assay results from its 50,000-metre 2026 drill program at the Golden Summit Project in the Fairbanks Mining District of Alaska, with six rigs simultaneously advancing metallurgical, infill, and step-out objectives. The most recent batch of results includes 336.8 metres averaging 1.32 g/t gold from 26.5 metres depth — representing approximately 444,600 gram-metres of gold in a single near-surface interval — alongside 131 metres at 1.48 g/t gold, 185.8 metres at 1.08 g/t gold, and a higher-grade intercept of 6.7 metres at 5.76 g/t gold. Golden Summit currently hosts an Indicated resource of 17.2 million ounces at 1.24 g/t gold (432 million tonnes) and an Inferred resource of 11.9 million ounces at 1.04 g/t (358 million tonnes), for a combined total approaching 30 million ounces — one of the largest undeveloped gold resources held by any TSX-listed junior developer. The 50,000-metre 2026 campaign is specifically designed to deliver an updated mineral resource estimate and advance the metallurgical, engineering, hydrogeological, and environmental baseline studies required for a 2027 pre-feasibility study on a defined, mineable portion of the 30-million-ounce system. The Fairbanks Mining District hosts Kinross's Fort Knox operation — a large-scale open-pit gold mine that has operated for three decades — providing proven regional infrastructure and a regulatory pathway for open-pit development at Golden Summit. For retail investors tracking large-resource bulk-tonnage gold development stories at $4,100+ gold, the steady six-rig assay cadence at Golden Summit produces the most consistent geological validation data of any single-deposit North American junior exploration program currently active.

headline: MERCADO MINERALS HITS 1,120 g/t SILVER EQUIVALENT OVER 1.2m AT COPALITO — NEW EL AGUA VEIN OPEN IN ALL DIRECTIONS IN SINALOA'S SAN DIMAS DISTRICT
source_name: Junior Mining Network / Mercado Minerals Ltd. (CSE: MERC) — June 18, 2026
snippet: Mercado Minerals Ltd. (CSE: MERC) reported additional results from the inaugural 3,000-metre diamond drill program at the Copalito polymetallic vein project in Sinaloa, Mexico on June 18, 2026 — with the El Agua Vein delivering 1.20 metres grading 34 g/t silver, 3.40 g/t gold, 19.00% lead, and 21.00% zinc (equivalent to 1,120 g/t silver) within a broader 3.50-metre interval grading 30 g/t silver, 1.94 g/t gold, 9.47% lead, and 14.61% zinc (686 g/t AgEq) from 124.75 metres depth. The El Agua Vein intersection was achieved through an aggressive step-out hole targeting a steeper structural interpretation, confirming the vein from a new geometric model and leaving mineralisation open in all directions — the geological configuration that historically precedes a focused multi-hole infill program on a newly defined blind vein. The 5 Señores Vein program was completed concurrently, with hole COP-26-009 returning 6.15 metres at 173 g/t AgEq (141 g/t silver, 0.40 g/t gold) from 83.55 metres, extending the productive strike length to approximately 800 metres and confirming vertical depth to approximately 125 metres on that structure. Copalito is located in the San Dimas Mining District of Sinaloa — the same corridor that hosts First Majestic Silver's San Dimas operation, a region that has produced approximately 600 million ounces of silver historically from the same vein-hosted epithermal silver system type. For retail investors tracking small-cap CSE-listed silver explorers in a post-ATH correction environment at $64-68/oz silver, the El Agua Vein's 1,120 g/t AgEq in 1.2 metres represents bonanza-grade silver mineralisation in a corridor where such grades have historically defined the fingerprint of blind vein systems large enough to support future mine development — and in a geological district that has already proven its capacity to host operating mines.

headline: ENDEAVOUR SILVER TERRONERA DRILL HINTS AT MINE-LIFE EXTENSION — 282 g/t Ag OVER 10m IN FIRST EXPLORATION HOLES AT OPERATING MEXICO MINE SINCE 2020
source_name: GlobeNewswire / Endeavour Silver Corp. (TSX: EDR; NYSE American: EXK) — June 18, 2026
snippet: Endeavour Silver Corp. (TSX: EDR; NYSE American: EXK) announced on June 18, 2026 the results of the first exploration drill program at its Terronera silver-gold mine in Jalisco, Mexico since 2020 — targeting both the Terronera vein extension and the adjacent La Luz system, whose production is targeted to begin in 2027. The standout intercepts from the Terronera vein component include hole TRU-001 returning 10 metres grading 282 g/t silver and 1.8 g/t gold from approximately 121 metres depth, and hole TRU-003 intersecting 9 metres at 150 g/t silver and 6.3 g/t gold from approximately 109 metres — both intersecting mineralisation outside the current Terronera mine plan and representing direct mine-life extension potential if vein continuity at these grades is confirmed through follow-up drilling. The La Luz system exploration program has completed 43 drill holes totalling 7,015 metres, with a separate 10-hole, 1,904-metre Terronera vein component; two drill rigs are currently active and will continue testing strike and depth extensions through Q4 2026. Terronera began production in late 2024 as Endeavour Silver's newest operating mine, making the June 18 results the first systematic confirmation that mine-life extension is geologically viable through near-mine exploration at the current $65-68/oz silver price. For retail investors tracking operating silver producers with production growth optionality, the Terronera mine-life extension results represent the highest-conviction near-term catalyst available to Endeavour Silver shareholders: the geological validation of additional mineable ounces at an operating mine with existing processing infrastructure directly increases the project's NPV without any incremental capital expenditure beyond the ongoing exploration drill budget.

headline: CRITICAL METALS STARTS 10,000m DRILL AT WORLD'S LARGEST UNDEVELOPED HREE DEPOSIT — TANBREEZ GREENLAND PILOT PLANT RISING, DAILY JET SERVICE ACTIVE
source_name: Mining Weekly (June 18, 2026) / Critical Metals Corp. (NASDAQ: CRML)
snippet: Critical Metals Corp. (NASDAQ: CRML) commenced a 10,000-metre diamond core drilling program at the Tanbreez Rare Earth Project in southern Greenland in June 2026, following the Greenland government's April 17, 2026 approval of the final 50.5% ownership transfer — bringing Critical Metals to 92.5% total ownership of one of the world's largest known undeveloped heavy rare earth element (HREE) resources. The Tanbreez deposit encompasses an estimated 4.7 billion tonnes at approximately 0.40% total rare earth oxides (REO), with the deposit's particular importance lying in its concentration of dysprosium (Dy) and terbium (Tb) — the two HREEs most critical for high-performance NdFeB permanent magnets used in EV motors, wind turbines, and defence guidance systems, and the specific elements most constrained by China's progressive export restriction regime since April 2023. The June 2026 drill program represents Critical Metals' first systematic diamond core drilling program at the Tanbreez scale: the 10,000-metre campaign targets multiple priority mineralised zones to establish an initial NI 43-101/JORC-compliant resource estimate from systematic core drilling data rather than the historical exploration datasets that have defined Tanbreez's dimensions to date. Simultaneously, infrastructure footings for the pilot plant headquarters are under construction near Qaqortoq International Airport, bulk sample preparations have begun for pilot plant metallurgical testing, and additional drill rigs are staged and ready for deployment pending initial results. Daily jet service between Qaqortoq and the project site has been established to maintain drilling momentum through the summer season. Against the backdrop of China's continuing export restriction regime targeting Dy, Tb, gallium, and germanium — and the US Strategic Critical Minerals Reserve's Project Vault ($10 billion in Ex-Im Bank financing targeting exactly this type of project) — a 92.5%-owned, 10,000-metre drilling program at the world's largest undeveloped HREE resource in a NATO-aligned Greenland jurisdiction is precisely the asset that Western governments' critical mineral security frameworks are structured to finance and accelerate.

headline: PREMIER AMERICAN URANIUM EXPANDS KAYCEE ROLL FRONTS IN POWDER RIVER BASIN — 19 HOLES COMPLETE IN 100,000 ft ISR SEASON ACROSS 36-MILE WYOMING TREND
source_name: GlobeNewswire / Premier American Uranium Inc. (TSX: PAU) — June 17, 2026
snippet: Premier American Uranium Inc. (TSX: PAU) released initial 2026 drill results from the Kaycee Project in Wyoming's Powder River Basin on June 17, 2026, with 19 drill holes totalling 17,100 feet completed at the Outpost target as part of a planned 100,000-foot 2026 exploration season targeting the Outpost, Rustler, and Stampede areas. Infill and step-out drilling has expanded and further defined the zone of known uranium mineralisation at the Outpost target. The Kaycee Project consists of over 42 square miles of mineral rights across a 36-mile mineralized trend hosting more than 110 miles of identified roll fronts — the classic in-situ recovery (ISR) uranium deposit geometry that characterises the most economically attractive and environmentally low-impact uranium production methodology available in Wyoming and the US Southwest. ISR uranium extraction uses no underground mining and produces no mill tailings; the method dissolves uranium in-place using groundwater solutions before recovering uranium-bearing solution at surface — the production method used by all operating uranium mines in Wyoming and the approach prioritised in the US Department of Energy's domestic uranium procurement program. The Powder River Basin's uranium mineralisation is structurally analogous to the ISR deposits already in production at Uranium One, Boss Energy, and enCore Energy operations in Wyoming and South Dakota, making the basin's geology well-understood and the permitting pathway for ISR projects more predictable than conventional hard-rock alternatives. For retail uranium investors tracking domestic US supply development ahead of the under-contracted 2030s utility demand cycle, Kaycee's 100,000-foot 2026 program represents the most intensive single-season drilling investment in the project's history — timed to the uranium spot market holding near $86/lb and the accelerating US utility contracting cycle that is creating urgency for new domestic supply commitments through 2028-2030.

headline: GOLDSILVER.COM: THE CORRECTION WAS THE SETUP — SILVER'S SIXTH DEFICIT YEAR MAKES JUNE 2026 THE STRUCTURAL ENTRY, NOT THE EXIT
snippet: GoldSilver.com's June 2026 silver price outlook analysis, titled 'The Correction Was the Setup,' presents the contrarian case for why silver's 47% decline from the January 2026 all-time high of approximately $121/oz to the current $64-68/oz range represents the structural accumulation opportunity rather than the beginning of a multi-year bear market. The core thesis rests on the fundamental incongruity between silver's technical condition — down 47% from ATH, below the 200-day moving average, gold-to-silver ratio near 62-64:1 — and the unchanged (in fact, deepening) structural supply-demand dynamics: the Silver Institute's 2026 World Silver Survey projects the sixth consecutive annual market deficit at approximately 46.3 million ounces, underpinned by record industrial demand from solar photovoltaics (each solar panel requires approximately 100mg of silver per watt of capacity), EV components, and semiconductor manufacturing, while primary silver mine supply has not materially increased despite three years of elevated silver prices prior to the January 2026 ATH. The analysis specifically addresses the Federal Reserve's hawkish June 2026 dot-plot (9 of 19 FOMC members projecting rate hikes) as the proximate cause of the correction while distinguishing between the rate-sensitive overlay and the physical supply-demand reality: the sixth consecutive annual deficit is not reversed by a Fed dot-plot revision. The gold-to-silver ratio expanding from 46:1 at the January ATH to 62-64:1 in June is highlighted as a statistically extreme reading that has historically marked the highest-conviction tactical entry points for silver relative to gold — the precursor to silver's characteristic phase of dramatically outperforming gold when the macro headwind resolves. For retail investors in TSXV and ASX-listed silver explorers and developers, the analysis frames the June 2026 correction as the entry condition — not the continuation signal — for the structural silver bull market thesis built on six years of consecutive deficit accumulation.

headline: CRUX INVESTOR: DATA CENTRES + MINE DISRUPTIONS + SECTION 232 = THE 2026 COPPER CRUNCH — 600,000-TONNE DEFICIT DEAD AHEAD
snippet: A Crux Investor analysis titled 'Mine Supply Disruptions & Section 232 Tariff Risk Tighten Copper Markets Ahead of a Forecast 600,000-Tonne 2026 Deficit' maps three structural forces converging to tighten copper markets through the second half of 2026: the widening annual supply deficit (Morgan Stanley forecasting 600,000 tonnes, J.P. Morgan 330,000 tonnes, ICSG 150,000 tonnes — the widest dispersion in analyst deficit forecasts in the copper market's recent history), specific mine supply disruptions reducing 2026 output from existing operations (Mongolia's Oyu Tolgoi political blockade, South American rainfall impacts, and Indonesian ore processing constraints), and the June 30 US Section 232 refined copper tariff report deadline that could structurally widen the COMEX-LME spread from the current approximately $400 per tonne to a potential $2,000+ per tonne premium for domestic US copper producers. The data centre demand angle is central to the analysis: a single large-scale AI data centre (100-200 MW capacity) requires approximately 2,000-4,000 tonnes of copper for power distribution, cooling infrastructure, and structural wiring — meaning the committed pipeline of 150+ hyperscale data centres under construction in North America in 2026 consumes a copper equivalent approaching 300,000-600,000 tonnes, a demand increment that was entirely absent from consensus demand forecasts published before 2024. For copper investors evaluating the investment case at the current LME price of approximately $13,000-$13,400 per tonne ($5.90-$6.08/lb), the analysis provides a specific forward scenario: a supply-deficit-justified LME price of $14,000-$15,000 per tonne layered over a potential $2,000+ US domestic tariff premium for North American copper producers — a combined scenario implying COMEX copper prices well above the May 2026 record of $6.65/lb, with British Columbia porphyry copper projects, US Southwest copper deposits, and Alaska VMS systems disproportionately benefiting from the tariff-driven premium relative to LME-priced international competitors.

headline: GOLD, SILVER, PLATINUM AND PALLADIUM ALL FIND PRICE FLOORS DESPITE FED HEADWINDS — INN: SUPPLY-DEMAND FUNDAMENTALS PROVIDE DURABLE SUPPORT
source_name: Investing News Network — Precious Metals Price Update, June 20-21, 2026
snippet: Investing News Network's June 2026 precious metals price update documents a convergence across all four precious metals — gold, silver, platinum, and palladium — in which supply-demand fundamentals are providing durable price floors even as near-term macro headwinds (Fed hawkishness, dollar strength) push prices toward those floors. Gold fell to approximately $4,150 on June 20, its lowest level since June 11, and is tracking a third consecutive weekly decline as the Federal Reserve's June 16-17 dot-plot (9 of 19 FOMC members projecting rate hikes) drove the US dollar to its highest level since May 2025. Silver dropped sharply in the immediate aftermath of the June 17 FOMC release before recovering approximately 70% of the loss — a recovery profile that INN attributes to physical buying absorbing speculative liquidation at the sub-$65 level. Platinum and palladium, often overlooked in precious metals coverage dominated by gold and silver, are demonstrating specific supply-demand dynamics: platinum supply has been constrained by South African mining disruptions and declining output from the Bushveld Complex, while palladium's ongoing demand from catalytic converter applications (still the dominant end-use despite EV penetration) is absorbing South African and Russian supply uncertainty. The World Gold Council's finding that a record 45% of central banks plan to add gold in the next 12 months is cited as the single most durable demand signal across all precious metals: central bank gold buying does not reverse on Fed dot-plot signals — it is a multi-year structural accumulation program that continues independent of the near-term rate trajectory. For retail investors managing precious metals exposure through the June 2026 correction, the INN analysis provides the key differentiation: the price pressure is macro-driven and rate-sensitive, while the price floor is fundamental and demand-driven — a combination that historically resolves in favour of the fundamental demand floor once the macro overhang clears.

headline: DEVERE GROUP: MINING STOCKS IN A BIFURCATED MARKET — GOLD EQUITIES AT RECORD FREE CASH FLOW MARGINS WHILE BATTERY METALS DRAG ON SENTIMENT
snippet: A deVere Group 2026 mining sector analysis framed as 'Investing in a Bifurcated Mining Market' identifies a fundamental split in the mining equity landscape that is creating confusion for generalist investors who view mining stocks as a single asset class: the gold and copper segments of the sector are operating at or near record free cash flow margins (gold producers at $4,100+ gold generating $2,750-$3,050 per ounce FCF margins; copper producers at $6.00+/lb generating record margins against $1.50-$2.50/lb AISC), while the battery metals segment — particularly lithium and nickel equities — continues to trade at multi-year lows as production oversupply persists through 2026 and spot lithium carbonate prices remain well below breakeven for high-cost producers. This bifurcation is directly relevant for retail investors in junior mining equities because it means that conventional sector-level sentiment metrics (e.g., the broad TSX Global Mining Index, or Bloomberg's BCOM Metals Index) are averaging across two fundamentally opposite operating environments and producing readings that accurately reflect neither. Specifically, the deVere analysis argues that gold and copper junior equities are being incorrectly discounted by generalist investors who see weak battery metals performance and assign a 'mining is weak' narrative to the entire sector — creating a valuation gap between gold and copper juniors' fundamental economics and their equity market pricing that represents an asymmetric opportunity for investors who understand the bifurcation. The framework has direct implications for portfolio construction: a TSXV-listed gold developer at $4,100 gold generating exploration results at an existing multi-million-ounce resource is not comparable to a TSXV-listed lithium developer facing years of oversupply, but generic 'junior mining ETF' exposure conflates both — making stock-specific selection in the gold and copper junior segment the most defensible approach to the sector in 2026.
